editorial:
Imagine being a couples therapist who has to use her own messy breakup history to fix other people's marriages. That is exactly what you get here. You follow a lead character who looks back at three very different exes: a guy she still has crazy chemistry with, a sweet artist, and a man who seemed way too perfect to be real. The vibe is cozy and emotional, making you feel like you are sitting in on a private therapy session. It is a sweet look at how our past mistakes actually teach us how to love better in the present.

The acting feels very natural, and the way the story jumps between the present and the past keeps things moving quickly. You will love how the movie handles the emotional growth of the characters, though some might find the pacing a bit slow in the middle. If you are in the mood for a heartfelt story, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: Everything comes together when the therapist realizes she was holding onto her exes to avoid her own growth. In the final scenes, she helps the struggling couple find a breakthrough by admitting her own flaws. She finally lets go of her past lovers to embrace a healthier version of herself. The movie wraps up with her finding a new, genuine connection, proving that you have to love yourself before you can truly love someone else.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves romantic dramas about second chances and self-discovery.
